content: Sulconazole is a topical medication prescribed to treat specific skin infections, including athlete's foot (cream formulation only), jock itch, and ringworm. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Sulconazole is available as a cream or solution for application to the skin. It is typically used once or twice daily, in the morning and evening, for a duration of 2 to 4 weeks. Certain infections may require up to 6 weeks of treatment. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use sulconazole exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than prescribed. Before application, thoroughly clean the affected area, allow it to dry, and gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication. Continue using sulconazole even if your symptoms improve. Do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Before using sulconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sulconazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using sulconazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sulconazole may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: itching, rash, burning, irritation or stinging, or redness. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Sulconazole is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of sulconazole, contact your doctor.
